sideboard_access.why: All 12 distinct sideboard cards are artifacts and Karn's -2 puts any of them from outside the game into hand, so the board is reached by tutor rather than by swapping. Physically siding a card in REMOVES it from Karn's pool: a card moved into the maindeck is no longer outside the game, so every physical swap trades tutorable breadth for the ability to draw one specific answer before a four-mana Karn resolves. play_plan.posture_why: answer the graveyard and Atraxa first, then out-size the fair half with Ugin.

sideboard_audit.why: The Tron-mana trump: 8/8 trample that destroys a nonland permanent on cast and again on each attack. It is the only card in the 75 that answers a resolved Emrakul, the Promised End, because it is a colorless permanent ability rather than a spell, so protection from instants does not stop it; against esper control it is the inevitability that grinds a Teferi, a Frog or a White Orchid Phantom off the board every attack.

The only clean answer to a named combo piece, and the widest Karn target in the pool: Consign to Memory against dimir, Basking Broodscale, Karn in the mirror, Ruby Medallion, Amulet of Vigor, and Devoted Druid against both the `creatures toolbox` and `devoted combo` halves of the same deck, where the second clause is the whole point - the {T}: Add {G} is a mana ability and survives, the untap-for-a-counter that makes the mana unbounded does not - and Urza's Saga, whose granted Construct ability it shuts off even though the tax half is dead against a land.

The widest fetch in the pool by share: Atraxa, Griselbrand, Primeval Titan, a boros board, a prowess board, Territorial Kavu and Hollow One all stop. It shuts most of ours off too - six cards in hand for Devourer, four for Thought-Knot, two for Fleshraker - so it is a stall, not a lock, and we win under it with Ugin, Fleshraker damage or Karn.

Sweeper and noncreature answer in one card at eight mana. The destroy half is noncreature-only, so it is aimed at Damping Sphere and Urza's Saga-style permanents rather than at threats; the 4 damage is what clears a boros or prowess board. It comes off the eldrazi ramp list on purpose - it moves neither Emrakul nor Ulamog.

Two copies because it is one of the two cards NOTES sanctions physically boarding, so the first is drawn and the second fetched. It does exactly two things - creature cards cannot enter from a graveyard or library, and nobody casts from either - which covers Goryo's Vengeance, Persist, Vengevine, the Neoform/Eldritch Evolution half of allosaurus combo, and - the widest of them - four Green Sun's Zenith, four Nature's Rhythm, Fiend Artisan and Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler's -2 in every list of the `creatures toolbox` and `devoted combo` rows, which are one deck under two archetype ids and so pay it twice. It does NOT cover living end, which is why that row is not on this list: cascade casts from exile and Living End returns creatures from exile, so neither clause is ever touched there.

The fetchable lifelinked blocker that races burn and aggro: a 6/6 deathtouch and lifelink body Karn hands us against the fast half of the field, and two 3/3 tokens through a sweeper or an artifact-removal spell when it dies. It ends a race Ensnaring Bridge only stalls, which is why it is the aggro-segment pickup rather than a second lock piece.

The cheap enchantment answer rather than the only one - the maindeck has eight at seven mana - and the reason to fetch it is that it costs {2} when seven is out of reach, notably under a Blood Moon at mana value 3. At zero counters it is also the sweeper against pinnacle affinity's free artifacts. Slow, and at 3 it destroys our own Fleshraker, Trinisphere and a fetched Bridge.

Nothing else in the 75 touches a card still in their library. It names Emrakul against eldrazi ramp, Living End, Primeval Titan and Past in Flames. Sorcery speed only, and it counters nothing in response, so it is used proactively on our own turn or not at all.

Free, so it is the graveyard answer castable under a Trinisphere or off one land, and it fires in response to Goryo's Vengeance or Persist targeting rather than needing to pre-empt them. It is the redundancy behind two Grafdigger's Cage, not a duplicate of them.

The pre-emptive answer to Solitude, Witch Enchanter, Flickerwisp, Ephemerate loops and Archon of Cruelty, and the only one that also blanks Witch Enchanter's own enters trigger. Its cost to us is asymmetric and worse than it looks - Thought-Knot keeps the leaves trigger that draws them a card - so it is fetched when their enters triggers are genuinely the problem, not by default. Against the `creatures toolbox` and `devoted combo` halves of the Devoted Druid deck those triggers are the earthbend on four Badgermole Cub in every list, the Craterhoof Behemoth pump in eight of ten, and Chomping Changeling's destroy-an-artifact trigger in five of ten of the current lists.

The second copy is both the standard combo fetch and the one card the plan physically boards on the play, because this deck has more three-plus spells than any fair opponent. It taxes storm rituals, cascade, one-mana disruption, Ephemerate and two zero-mana Pacts; on the draw against a fair deck it is the card most often left in the board.

Scalable removal and the answer to a one-toughness board: Ocelot Pride, Guide of Souls, Ragavan, Dragon's Rage Channeler, Emissary Drones, Orcish Bowmasters, Psychic Frog and Harbinger of the Seas all die to one or two counters. The broadest cheap fetch across the aggro half of the field.

deck_tech.name: Chalice of the Void: which number
deck_tech.quirk: X is chosen on cast and never again, so the number is a read on their curve rather than a default.

lines.why: Mox Opal, Mishra's Bauble, Claws of Gix and Welding Jar are all free. Living End has no mana cost, so its mana value is 0 and zero counters the cascaded copy. Cash our own Vexing Bauble before casting it.
Their one-mana spells outnumber our answers. It counters our own Expedition Map and Vexing Bauble too, so set it once the lands are already found and the Bauble has been cashed.

Goryo's Vengeance and both storm rituals are two mana; against the Devoted Druid deck two catches Devoted Druid, Badgermole Cub, Vizier of Remedies and a post-board Collector Ouphe. Cast the two-mana Karn fetches BEFORE this resolves.

lines.mode: X=1 on the play, X=2 on the draw
lines.why: On the play one catches their whole turn-one suite. On the draw it lands after the damage is done, and two for Psychic Frog, Ajani or Goblin Bombardment is worth more.
Only once Blood Moon is the card beating us. Three also blanks our own three Fleshraker, two Dismember, Trinisphere and a fetched Ensnaring Bridge: a trade, not an upgrade.
Against a curve of one and four-plus it costs us more than it costs them, and a number we have already named is a number we cannot change.

deck_tech.name: Vexing Bauble: the three casts of OURS it counters
deck_tech.quirk: The trigger is 'whenever A PLAYER casts a spell, if no mana was spent' - it does not care whose spell it is, and this deck casts three things for no mana.

lines.mode: sacrifice it before the zero-mana Karn fetch
lines.why: Karn's -2 puts Tormod's Crypt or a Walking Ballista for X=0 into hand and our own Bauble counters both. Cash it for the card in response to the Karn activation, not after the fetch is already in hand.

lines.mode: Chalice on 0 and the Bauble are the same slot
lines.why: A Chalice cast for X=0 spends no mana, so our own Bauble counters it. Pick one: against living end the Bauble already counters the payoff, so the Chalice is redundant there.
The -11 casts colorless cards without paying their mana costs, which is no mana spent, so the Bauble counters every one of them. Sacrifice it for the card before the ultimate resolves.

deck_tech.name: Which lock piece goes down
deck_tech.quirk: Both are symmetric and both tax us, so the question is which one and whether either is worth it at all.

lines.why: The one card worth a physical swap: we need to draw it before a four-mana Karn resolves. Weakest on the draw, and against a fair deck it stays in the board.

lines.mode: Ensnaring Bridge, once our hand is spent
lines.why: Their creatures are one to three power and ours are bigger. Power greater than OUR hand size cannot attack, so it goes down empty-handed, not on turn three holding six.

lines.mode: Bridge as a stall we still have to win under
lines.why: Under our own Bridge, Devourer needs six cards in hand to attack and Thought-Knot four. Win through it with Ugin, Fleshraker damage or Karn, not with combat.
A symmetric lock piece taxes the player with more cheap spells, and against a deck we are already ahead of, that is us.

deck_tech.name: Which of our two engines this matchup is
deck_tech.quirk: The deck has an artifact lock and a colourless top end, and most hands only get to run one of them.

lines.why: Karn's static blanks most of their seventy-five and the minus two reaches twelve answers from outside the game. Against artifact decks it is the whole plan.

Ugin exiles a coloured permanent on every colourless spell we cast and grinds their rebuys down, and All Is Dust answers a coloured board; against these decks our bigger colourless top end wins, not the Karn lock.

lines.mode: Fleshraker and its Spawn as a clock
lines.why: Fleshraker plus a Spawn stabilises where a seven-drop does not. A Spawn held is mana for a later Ugin turn; a Spawn cashed is gone, so do not sacrifice them to use them.

meta_calls.why: A room of one-drops makes a fourth Chalice on one the card that wins alone; the sideboard already carries Wurmcoil Engine for the race Ensnaring Bridge only stalls, so only the maindeck Chalice moves.
meta_calls.cost: Chalice named on one counters our own Vexing Bauble, so the fourth copy and the Bauble cannot both sit in the sixty: the free-spell answer is what the aggro hedge is bought with.

meta_calls.why: Blast Zone with the counter it enters with destroys Amulet of Vigor, the permanent that turns their bounce lands into a turn-two Titan. Karn tutors artifacts, so only a land reaches this.
meta_calls.cost: A colourless source that always taps becomes one that costs two to use, in a deck whose curve is already colourless-hungry.

meta_calls.why: Consign counters a colourless spell or a triggered ability, and every spell in this sixty is colourless. Cavern naming Eldrazi makes eleven of them uncounterable and still taps for colourless.
meta_calls.cost: Twenty-three lands, no sweeper in the sixty, and a land that does not assemble Tron in place of the basic that survives Harbinger. Cavern protects creature spells only, so All Is Dust was never one of the eleven.

meta_calls.why: Under Harbinger every land taps for blue only and the deck stops casting. Dismember is payable off one Island plus four life, so it still answers the Harbinger.
meta_calls.cost: All Is Dust is the only sweeper in the sixty and Karn cannot fetch it; Emrakul goes with it, and under a resolved Harbinger every land taps for blue only, so neither was castable anyway.

meta_calls.why: A turn-two 4/4 off Eldrazi Temple blocks and strips a card; a nine-drop needs a game that reaches turn nine. When the field kills before it, the fourth Seer is worth more than the haymaker.
meta_calls.cost: Emrakul is the only inevitability against a grindy fair deck and one of nine Ugin's Labyrinth imprints; the fourth Seer is the weakest in a topdeck war, and its leaves trigger gives them a card.

meta_calls.why: Basking Broodscale's adapt and Devoted Druid's untap are activated abilities of CREATURES, and Karn's static only reaches artifacts. Totem covers the one gap the lock has against all three engines.
meta_calls.cost: Symmetric, and we are not clean: it blanks our own Walking Ballista and every Eldrazi Spawn token's Sacrifice: Add {C}, which is the mana Glaring Fleshraker and Kozilek's Command make.

gaps.why: Break the Ice ({B}{B}, overload {4}{B}{B}) destroys each land that could produce {C}; overloaded that is 21 of our 22 lands, and there is no answer to it in the 75. Three copies in a board we pulled (tournament 9518c175-dc15-4b8f-b81d-d9d6b14227fd). The plan is to have already resolved a Karn or a Ugin, which is a race, not an answer. Harbinger of the Seas compounds it from the other side.

Damping Sphere is in every board we pulled and no card in the 75 reaches it: Karn's static does not (it has no activated ability), no mode of Kozilek's Command answers an artifact, and Devourer, Ugin and All Is Dust all read 'one or more colors'. The only outs are the eight-mana pair, which is exactly what a resolved Damping Sphere stops us from casting.

The matchup the Karn plan is worst against. Everything Karn fetches is an artifact and Witch Enchanter ({3}{W}, destroy target artifact or enchantment on entry) is a 3-4 of rebought by Ephemerate, Phelia and Flickerwisp, which is why Ensnaring Bridge is recorded BLANKED here. Clarion Conqueror turns Karn's own abilities off, and Damping Sphere is in 2 of the 3 boards we pulled with no answer in the 75.
